page: Microsoft Azure E32bs_v6 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by an Intel processor, the instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs coupled with 256.0 GB of system memory. This configuration maintains a 1:8 compute-to-RAM ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, designed for applications requiring substantial working memory per thread without shared-core interference.

A defining aspect of the Ebsv6 family architecture is its optimization for remote block storage performance. The E32bs_v6 comes with no local ephemeral storage included, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage disks for both operating system and operational data. This architectural tradeoff eliminates local disk management overhead and host-bound ephemeral constraints, prioritizing consistent remote I/O throughput to managed storage volumes. Hardware accelerators are omitted, with zero GPUs present.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance eliminates overhead associated with unneeded local NVMe storage and specialized accelerator silicon, focusing resource allocation strictly on high memory density and dedicated core execution. The server fits production database engines, distributed caching clusters, enterprise resource planning platforms, and intensive transaction processing environments that decouple compute from persistent disk tiers.
description: Microsoft Azure E32bs_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on x86_64 Intel processor architecture, managed through Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs alongside 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-heavy operations. As an Ebsv6 series machine, it focuses on high remote block storage throughput and supports Premium Storage disks, but omits integrated local scratch storage. Acceleration hardware is not included, featuring zero GPUs. Operating without included public IPv4 addresses or local disk overhead, the resource profile prioritizes dense memory capacity and scalable external storage attachment over local ephemeral drives. This architecture provides reliable performance efficiency for large relational database management systems, in-memory caches, enterprise ERP deployments, and transactional data processing environments that rely entirely on decoupled, persistent network block storage.
